text: Paulus, et Silvanus, et Timotheus, Thessalonicensium ecclesiae, quae Dei Patris nostri est, et Domini Jesu Christi,
note: *Patris* capital, God the Father (ἐν Θεῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν, NRSV \"God our Father\"; decision 20), *nostrī* lower case, as 1 Thess 1:1 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Gratiam et pacem a Deo Patre nostro, et Domino Jesu Christo.
note: *Grātiam* keeps its capital: the greeting is its own clause after the address of 1:1, as Gal 1:3, your 1 Cor 1:3 and 2 Cor 1:2 (the latter after 2 Cor 1:1's comma), written here because the pipeline would lower it after 1:1's comma (1573 *gratiam*, which lowers every verse start); *Patre* capital, God the Father (decision 20), as 1 Thess 1:1 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Deo gratias agere debemus immortales de vobis, fratres, ut dignum est, quod adeo crescit vestra fides, adeoque exuberat vestrum omnium mutua caritas,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): the thanksgiving (1:3–12) after the greeting, as 1 Thess 1:2 and your Phil 1:3, Col 1:3; *cāritās,* with a comma, as 1573 (*mutua charitas , 4 vt nosipſi*, canvas 907), for the draft's full stop: 1:4's *Ut nōs ipsī … glōriēmur* is the result of 1:3 (ὥστε ἡμᾶς αὐτοὺς … καυχᾶσθαι), so it starts in lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Eam ob rem nos semper pro vobis oramus, ut vos Deus eo, in quem vocati estis, statu dignos reddat, perficiatque, ut bonitatem ac fidei opus, et libentissime et fortiter persequamini atque absolvatis,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:10 ends the sentence on the judgment (1:5–10) and *Eam ob rem nōs semper prō vōbīs ōrāmus* turns to Paul's prayer (1:11–12); *absolvātis,* with a comma, as 1573 (*atq; abfoluatis , 12 quo Domini*, canvas 907), for the draft's full stop: 1:12's *Quō … celebrētur* is the purpose of the prayer (ὅπως ἐνδοξασθῇ), so it starts in lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Rogamus autem vos, fratres, quod attinet ad adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi, et nostri ad eum adgregationem,
note: *aggregātiōnem,* with a comma, as 1573 (*ad eum aggregationem , 2 ne citò*, canvas 907), for the draft's full stop: *Rogāmus … nē … dīmoveāminī* is one sentence (ἐρωτῶμεν … εἰς τὸ μὴ … σαλευθῆναι), the request and its content, so 2:2 starts in lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nemo vos ullo modo decipiat: nam non prius id futurum est, quam venerit defectio, et patefactus fuerit homo flagitiosus, homo ille perditus,
note: *perditus,* with a comma, as 1573 (*homo ille perditus , 4 qui aduerfatur*, canvas 907), for the draft's full stop: 2:4 describes the man of 2:3 (ὁ ἀντικείμενος, in apposition), so it starts in lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: qui adversatur, et se supra quidquid dicitur deus, aut numen, extollit: adeo, ut in Dei templo tamquam Deus sedeat, sese Deum esse ostendens.
note: *deus* lower case, \"every so-called god\" (ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον θεόν, NRSV \"every so-called god\"), a god of the nations, not God, as your 2 Cor 4:4 *hujus sæculī deus* and Phil 3:19 *prō deō*; 1573 prints *Deus*, which capitalizes the word everywhere; *Deī templō* and *tamquam Deus … Deum* stay capital, the true God whose place he claims; *quī* lower case, the sentence of 2:3 running on (written here, as a changed capital stops the pipeline's own lowering) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Tum demum exsistet ille scelerosus, quem Dominus oris sui spiritu conficiet, adventusque sui claritate delebit:
note: *spīritū* lower case: the breath of his mouth (τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, NRSV \"the breath of his mouth\", after Isa 11:4, left unmarked as an allusion), not the Holy Spirit (decision 20), as 1573 (*oris ſui ſpiritu*, canvas 908), for the draft's capital (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ipse vero Dominus noster Jesus Christus, et Deus Pater noster, qui nos pro suo favore adamavit, aeternoque solatio et bona spe donavit,
note: *Pater* capital, God the Father (ὁ Θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ ἡμῶν; decision 20), *noster* lower case, as 1 Thess 3:11 *Ipse Deus Paterque noster* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Salutatio mea manu Pauli, quod signum est in omnibus epistolis. Sic scribo:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): Paul's own hand closing the letter, as your Col 4:18 and 1 Cor 16:21 *Salūtātiō mea Paulī manū* open theirs (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Adsit vobis omnibus Domini nostri Jesu Christi gratia: Amen. \\cls Scripta Athenis.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 sets it under the blessing (*gratia : Amen . Scripta Athenis .*, canvas 908) and as 1 Thess 5:28, Gal 6:18, Col 4:18; a full stop after it, as 1573 (the draft has none); *grātia: Āmēn.* with 1573's colon, as Col 4:18 and Eph 6:24 (Claude, 2026-11-11)
